 The conclusion to Denis Villeneuve's Dune trilogy is approaching. Anya Taylor-Joy returns in Dune: Part Three as Alia Atreides, sister of Paul Atreides (Timothee Chalamet), after debuting in the role in Paul's brief vision in Dune: Part Two . The siblings are seen together in a new image from the upcoming movie.
 The image, released by Empire , depicts Alia standing beside Paul as he sits on his throne as Padishah Emperor of the Known Universe. Paul won the throne, at great cost, at the conclusion of Dune: Part Two .
 Anya Taylor-Joy Returns as Alia Atreides in Dune: Part Three
 Introduced in Frank Herbert's original Dune novel, Alia becomes a main character in the saga's sequels, Dune Messiah (which Dune: Part Three adapts) and Children of Dune (which Villeneuve has said he has no interest in adapting).
 Alia is the daughter of Duke Leto Atreides and the Bene Gesserit Lady Jessica, making her Paul's younger sister. Jessica gave birth to Alia on the planet Arrakis months after Leto's death. Alia was born with the power and memory of an adult Bene Gesserit Reverend Mother. Her power makes her feared and a vital advisor to Paul. However, the Bene Gesserit consider Alia an abomination, and they still hold some sway in the universe, even under Paul's rule.
 Dune: Part Three Will Be "Very Different" From the First Two Movies
 Anya Taylor-Joy as Alia Atreides and Timothee Chalamet as Paul Atreides in  Dune: Part Three . Image via Empire Magazine 
 Alia's presence at Paul's side isn't the only difference between Dune: Part Three and its two predecessors . Paul claiming his full power and ascending the throne at the end of Dune: Part Two has changed the world entirely, as Dune: Part Three picks up the story 17 years later.
 “The idea was to try to make a movie that will have the same DNA — it’s a Dune movie — but it’s a very different movie,” Villeneuve told Empire. “It has a different pacing... We are back with the same characters, but this time the world has totally changed. Their psyches, their perspective on reality has totally changed, and Paul is living with the burden of what he created, trying to find a way out of this spiral of violence.”
 That means it is on Chalamet to develop Paul beyond the young man coming into his own and struggling with the weight of destiny that he played in Dune 's first two installments. But what does that make him now?
 “That phrase ‘anti-hero’ gets thrown around a little too loosely perhaps, but it’s fantastic to chew on as an actor, where it’s not purely redemptive,” Chalamet says. He also says that Dune: Part Three is “its own beast. It’s its own story, its own siege, its own hail of paranoid isolation.”

 Villeneuve also confirmed again that this would be his last trip to Arrakis . “I said, ‘Maybe it’s a good idea to go back to this project, not out of nostalgia, not because I miss it, but the opposite — I’m tired of it,’” he said. “I want to make sure that I will be severe with the material. That I will not be complacent. I thought, ‘When it’s done, I need a very powerful rocket to pull me away from Arrakis.’ When I was asked to do the next Bond, I said: ‘Okay, this is what I need.’”
 Dune: Part Three opens in theaters on Dec. 18.
